A note from Cocoon

Wade, Jessica — here's how we're running the vendor side of your wedding so you don't have to.

You're hosting 135 people for six hours of celebration at Casa Duende, and there's a lot of moving pieces — catering in two phases, a bar program, a DJ, and the logistics that tie it all together. Our job through SuperConcierge is to own that coordination end-to-end: sourcing the vendors, getting the quotes, vetting the options, and presenting you with clear choices rather than a pile of emails to sort through.

This document lays out the structure of the evening and where we are on each piece. Catering quotes are in — two vendor options are in front of you now, a third is on its way. DJ candidate is presenting, equipment is priced, and bar is next up. As each piece locks in, this proposal updates to show what we've confirmed.

Two Cocoon managers will be on-site the night of — your team is covered from vendor load-in to the last song.

— Eduard, Cocoon Flex Spaces

The venue · Casa Duende

Your home for the night — a Cocoon flex space with main floor, lobby, and rooftop terrace, wired for a full wedding reception.

Main Floor
The heart of the event — open layout for dining, cocktail hour, and dancing. Lounge seating and benches stay in place, keeping the footprint loose and social.
Capacity: 130 indoor · dance floor opens at 9 PM
Rooftop Terrace
Open-air overflow throughout the night — speeches, fresh air, quieter conversations. Rooftop grill on-site for licensed food handlers.

Lobby & Lounge
Connects to the main floor — seating clusters for guests who want to sit away from the speakers. Flows naturally in and out of the main space.

The space

Casa Duende has a main floor and lobby for the event, with lounge seating and benches that stay in place — the space keeps an open footprint for dancing. The rooftop terrace provides a natural overflow zone for speeches, fresh air, and quieter conversation moments throughout the night.

Catering · Two phases

A cocktail-hour grazing program.
Then late-night fuel for the dance floor.

The food program is structured in two acts — full-service elevated grazing for the cocktail hour, and a self-serve late-night drop-off when the dancing kicks in. Gluten-free and vegetarian options required throughout both phases.
